# tac

Print records in reverse order through MoonX.

## Usage

```sh
moonx cli/tac input.txt

printf 'one\ntwo\n' | moonx cli/tac

moonx cli/tac -s : input.txt
```

Use newline separators by default. Fixed-string mode reads backwards from files and spools non-seekable input.

## Common options

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OPTIONS -->
<!-- Generated by tools/metadata from options.json. -->

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-b`, `--before` | Attach separators to the following record. |
| `-s VALUE`, `--separator VALUE` | Set a separator; empty fixed separator means NUL. Default: `"\n"`. |
| `-r`, `--regex` | Interpret the separator using GNU Emacs byte regex syntax. |
| `--help` | Show help. |
| `--version` | Show the version. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

## Notes

Build from source with the MoonBit 1.0 RC1 toolchain.

- Regex separators use the supported C-locale Emacs-style grammar and retain the entire input, subject to Int32 size limits.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md) for the supported profile.
